label: Side by Side
title: Three Christian views of baptism, question by question
intro: All three baptize with water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, because Christ commanded it. They part over who should be baptized and what God does in it. Each cell follows the tradition's own confession.
image_title: Three Christian views of baptism, side by side
image_subtitle: Each answer follows the tradition's own confession.
image_subtitle_narrow: Each answer follows the tradition's own confession.
image_source: Sources: Baptist Faith and Message 2000, Art. VII; Second London Baptist Confession 29; Westminster Confession 28; Heidelberg Catechism Q74; Augsburg Confession IX; Luther's Small and Large Catechisms
caption: Baptist churches baptize those who profess faith, by immersion, as a sign of forgiveness already received. Presbyterian and Reformed churches baptize believers and their children, and Westminster says its grace is not tied to the moment it is given. Lutheran churches baptize infants and adults, and teach that through baptism God gives forgiveness to all who believe.

common_text: All three baptize adults who come to faith, with water, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, because Christ commanded it: "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19, ESV).
differ: Who receives it: Baptists baptize professing believers only; Presbyterian, Reformed and Lutheran churches also baptize believers' children.
Mode: Baptists require immersion; Westminster calls pouring or sprinkling proper; Luther's Small Catechism defines baptism as water joined to God's command and Word.

What God does: Baptists see a sign of forgiveness already received; Westminster says the Spirit confers grace to those it belongs to, in God's appointed time; Lutherans teach that baptism works forgiveness of sins and gives salvation to all who believe.
Necessity: the Augsburg Confession calls baptism necessary to salvation; Westminster says grace and salvation are not so bound to it that no one can be saved without it.
A Presbyterian or Lutheran who joins a Baptist church is baptized on profession of faith; Westminster and the Large Catechism hold that baptism is not repeated.
note: Cells paraphrase the confessions listed below the chart, with Stephen Wellum (Baptist) and the Heidelberg Catechism on the children row and Luther's Small and Large Catechisms in the Lutheran column. No view is presented here as the answer.

sources.title: The Baptist Faith and Message 2000
sources.quote: Christian baptism is the immersion of a believer in water in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. It is an act of obedience symbolizing the believer's faith in a crucified, buried, and risen Saviour
sources.notes: Art. VII also: "Being a church ordinance, it is prerequisite to the privileges of church membership and to the Lord's Supper." Rows: who, how, meaning, order, membership, examples.

sources.title: Second London Baptist Confession of Faith (1689), Chapter 29: Of Baptism
sources.quote: Those who do actually profess repentance towards God, faith in, and obedience to, our Lord Jesus Christ, are the only proper subjects of this ordinance.
sources.notes: 29.4: "Immersion, or dipping of the person in water, is necessary to the due administration of this ordinance." Rows: who, how, again (infant sprinkling does not meet 29.2 and 29.4). 29.1: baptism is "a sign of his fellowship with him, in his death and resurrection; of his being engrafted into him; of remission of sins" (row: god).

sources.title: The Westminster Confession of Faith, Chapter 28: Of Baptism
sources.quote: Not only those that do actually profess faith in and obedience unto Christ, but also the infants of one, or both, believing parents, are to be baptized.
sources.notes: 28.1 sign and seal of the covenant of grace, admission into the visible church; 28.3 "Dipping of the person into the water is not necessary; but baptism is rightly administered by pouring, or sprinkling water upon the person."; 28.5 not all baptized are regenerated; 28.6 "The efficacy of baptism is not tied to that moment of time wherein it is administered", grace conferred "in his appointed time" to such as that grace belongs to; 28.5 "grace and salvation are not so inseparably annexed unto it, as that no person can be regenerated, or saved, without it"; 28.7 "The sacrament of baptism is but once to be administered unto any person." Row god: 28.6, "by the right use of this ordinance, the grace promised is not only offered, but really exhibited, and conferred, by the Holy Ghost, to such (whether of age or infants) as that grace belongeth unto".

sources.publisher: Christian Reformed Church in North America
sources.title: Heidelberg Catechism, Q&A 74
sources.quote: This was done in the Old Testament by circumcision, which was replaced in the New Testament by baptism.
sources.notes: Row: covenant-sign (paedobaptist cell). Footnote numerals in the page text are omitted from the quote.

sources.title: Why I Am a Credobaptist (Justin Taylor's interview with Stephen Wellum)
sources.quote: All those who are "in Christ" are a regenerate people, and as such it is only they who may receive the sign of the covenant, namely baptism.
sources.notes: Row: covenant-sign (credobaptist cell). Wellum also: "Does circumcision signify the exact same spiritual realities as baptism? ... this is precisely what the NT does not teach." Posted November 11, 2011.

sources.title: Augsburg Confession, Article IX: Of Baptism
sources.quote: children are to be baptized who, being offered to God through Baptism are received into God's grace
sources.notes: Art. IX opens: "Of Baptism they teach that it is necessary to salvation, and that through Baptism is offered the grace of God". Rows: who, children; differ: necessity.

sources.title: Luther's Small Catechism, The Sacrament of Holy Baptism
sources.quote: It works forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives eternal salvation to all who believe this
sources.notes: Also: "Baptism is not simple water only, but it is the water comprehended in God's command and connected with God's Word" (row how); "It signifies that the old Adam in us should, by daily contrition and repentance, be drowned and die with all sins and evil lusts, and, again, a new man daily come forth and arise" (row meaning). Row god.

sources.title: Luther's Large Catechism, Part IV: Of Baptism
sources.quote: Baptism, however, is not our work, but God's
sources.notes: Para 10: "although it is performed by human hands, it is nevertheless truly God's own work" (row god). Para 57: "we do not baptize it upon that, but solely upon the command of God. Why so? Because we know that God does not lie." (row children). "no one should rebaptize them" (row again).
